headline: The entry-exception front is live: separate the clocks, then assign the rows before cargo enters.
dek: W30 weather is not one blended tariff score. USTR entry timing, India exemption math, Brazil stacking, freight, import pull-forward, pharma qualification, AI capacity and fuel each have separate owners, clocks and evidence files.

zones.name: USTR entry clock
zones.operator_meaning: USTR's forced-labor Section 301 final action became effective at 12:01 a.m. ET on 24 July 2026, with a transition cutoff at 12:01 a.m. ET on 28 July for qualifying goods loaded before the effective moment and entered before the cutoff.
zones.watch: CBP guidance, broker notes, disputes and USTR clarifications around product exemptions, country treatment and annex detail.

zones.name: Duty coverage
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters and FreightWaves reported 10% and 12.5% duty families across 60 trading partners, with coverage described as 99.4% of U.S. imports; USTR remains the source of record for legal decisions.
zones.watch: Do not use the public coverage number as a treatment decision; map affected country and product family to HTS, mechanism and exemption status.

zones.name: India exemption math
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters reported India faces a 10% rate while India's commerce ministry said about 45% of U.S.-bound exports remain outside the fresh duty and 55% face it.
zones.watch: Product-family split, exemption treatment, supplier proof and customer-price caveats for India-linked rows.

zones.name: Brazil stacking
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters reported a 25% U.S. tariff threatening $7 billion to $11 billion of Brazilian exports and possible 37.5% combined duty on some goods if the forced-labor layer applies.
zones.watch: Exposed, exempt, stacked and uncertain Brazil rows before finance refreshes landed cost or reserves.

zones.name: Freight station
zones.operator_meaning: Drewry's 23 July tracker put the World Container Index at $4,374 per 40-foot container, down 4%, and IACI at $960 per 40-foot container, down 2%.
zones.watch: Next Drewry readings and route detail, kept separate from tariff treatment and import-volume indicators.

zones.name: Import volume
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters, citing Descartes, reported June U.S. container imports up 8.2% year over year to 2,400,627 TEUs after buyers moved cargo early.
zones.watch: Whether July import strength becomes inventory overhang or sell-through-confirmed demand.

zones.name: Pharma qualification
zones.operator_meaning: Supply Chain Dive reported a generic-drug tariff ladder that would keep qualifying goods at 0% for two years from 1 August before much higher levies; Reuters generic context cited FDA that more than 90% of U.S. medicines are generics.
zones.watch: Formal text and qualification, validation, site, API and packaging workstream timing.

zones.name: AI infrastructure
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters reported Samsung and Broadcom cooperation expected to exceed $200 billion through 2030, while separate power-equipment reporting points to data-center grid equipment constraints.
zones.watch: Transformer, switchgear, memory, packaging and grid-access reservation updates.

zones.name: Fuel station
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters reported dated Brent at $105.70 and North Sea Forties at $108.77 on 24 July after supply disruptions.
zones.watch: Oil and fuel-surcharge movement as a separate cost station, not a container-rate claim.

reference_cards.label: USTR effective time
reference_cards.note: Forced-labor Section 301 final action effective time.

reference_cards.label: Transition cutoff
reference_cards.note: For qualifying goods loaded before the effective moment and entered before cutoff.

reference_cards.label: Duty families
reference_cards.note: Reuters/FreightWaves reported families across 60 trading partners; use USTR for legal scope.

reference_cards.label: India split
reference_cards.note: Reported exempt versus exposed U.S.-bound export share per Reuters.

reference_cards.label: Brazil exposure
reference_cards.note: Reuters reported export exposure and possible 37.5% combined duty on some goods.

reference_cards.label: Drewry WCI
reference_cards.note: 23 July tracker, down 4%; keep separate from import-volume signal.

reference_cards.label: June U.S. imports
reference_cards.note: Reuters/Descartes reported +8.2% year over year after early cargo movement.

reference_cards.label: Dated Brent
reference_cards.note: Reuters physical oil report, 24 July; fuel station only.

operator_translation: Do not blend the stations into a fake composite score. Build an entry exception board with one row per affected product, origin, HTS mechanism, exemption state, vessel or warehouse status, entry deadline, customer commitment and owner.
operator_watchlist: CBP guidance, broker notes or disputes before and after the 28 July transition cutoff.
USTR clarifications on product exemptions, country treatment and annex details.
India, Brazil, Australia or other trading-partner responses that change exemption or retaliation risk.
Formal text for the reported generic-drug tariff schedule before the 1 August plan start.
Drewry's next WCI and IACI readings, kept separate from Freightos, SONAR and carrier commentary unless a source combines them.
Reuters/Descartes, NRF/Hackett or port data showing whether import pull-forward becomes inventory overhang.
Oil and fuel-surcharge movement, kept separate from container spot rates.
AI infrastructure procurement updates for transformers, switchgear, memory, advanced packaging and grid access.

newsletter_insert.title: Supply Chain Weather
newsletter_insert.headline: Entry-exception weather: the clocks matter more than a composite score.
newsletter_insert.body: This week's weather map has separate stations for the USTR 24-28 July entry clock, broad 10% and 12.5% duty families, India exemption math, Brazil stacking, Drewry freight, import pull-forward, pharma qualification, AI infrastructure and fuel. They should not be blended into one risk number because each station has a different source, owner and clock.
newsletter_insert.operator_translation: Before the next planning meeting, create one entry exception board: product, origin, HTS, mechanism, exemption status, vessel status, entry deadline, customer commitment and named owner. External watch items stay external; internal action rows get owners.
